page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general purpose instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz with the x86_64 instruction set. The system provides 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 54 MB of L3 cache and instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AES-NI. System memory totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance bundles local storage via a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes show mid-tier single-threaded capabilities coupled with limited multi-core throughput due to the 2-core physical limit. Single-core performance achieves 1601.0 in Geekbench and 1892.08 in stress-ng, placing it within the middle 50% band. However, multi-core metrics such as the Geekbench multi-core score (3388.0) and PassMark CPU score (5883.55) fall into the bottom 25%. Memory throughput measures 30.03 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 25.36 GB/sec for write operations. Network throughput and static web serving register solid middle-tier capability at 6.34 GB/sec.

With integrated NVMe storage and balanced memory, the instance delivers a practical resource profile without requiring separate network storage volumes for temporary caching or scratch files. Tradeoffs include modest parallel compute capabilities and lower multi-threaded throughput. Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge fits general-purpose tasks such as small-to-midsize relational databases requiring local caching, web serving, microservices, and continuous integration agents.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 237 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage on the Nitro hypervisor platform. It features a baseline network speed of 6 Gbps and lacks discrete GPUs. Benchmarks reflect moderate single-thread execution, reaching 1601.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside a 6.34 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Multi-core performance lands in the lower 25% percentile due to the low physical core count, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 3388.0. The configuration provides balanced memory and high-speed local disk capacity, making it appropriate for web applications, staging environments, intermediate data processing, and lightweight database workloads.
